## Plannerly TL;DR

Plannerly is a cloud-based BIM management platform that consolidates fragmented construction workflows into an ISO 19650-compliant system for architecture, engineering, and construction firms. The platform automates project documentation, model validation, and standards compliance while supporting 80+ file formats. Its key differentiator is a storage-based pricing model that includes unlimited viewer access across all tiers—eliminating per-seat costs common in enterprise software—and a specialized focus on BIM execution planning and ISO 19650 standards rather than competing directly with general modeling tools.

## Plannerly Company Overview

Plannerly operates as a cloud-based platform addressing the construction industry's fragmented BIM workflows. The company [secured](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/plannerly/__J-D8i-wylqGr6ep6bHt9LEW_h90IHPC0LOT2E74kBlA/funding-and-investors) a $4.12 million Series A round led by Shadow Ventures in April 2025, positioning itself as a specialized management layer rather than a general-purpose construction software tool.

The platform tackles what construction teams waste hours on: disconnected tools for BIM management, manual documentation creation, and tedious model validation. [Plannerly](https://plannerly.com/) built its architecture specifically around ISO 19650 international standards—not as an afterthought, but as the central organizing principle.

The company holds [partnership status](https://www.autodesk.com/integrations/partner/plannerly) with Autodesk, suggesting a coopetition strategy: complementing rather than replacing modeling tools like Revit and Navisworks. This positions Plannerly as orchestration software that sits above modeling and clash detection tools, managing the execution planning and compliance workflows that construction firms need for complex projects.

Public information about founding date, leadership team, and company scale remains limited—typical for an early-stage private company. The recent Series A suggests the company is transitioning from initial product development to market expansion.

## Plannerly Product Features

[Plannerly](https://plannerly.com/) consolidates BIM project management into a single platform with three core capabilities:

**Automated Compliance & Validation**

The platform handles [automated model checking](https://plannerly.com/product) across 80+ file formats—saving teams from manual validation that eats entire workdays. Built-in ISO 19650 compliance tools enforce standards automatically rather than requiring BIM managers to memorize and manually apply specifications.

**Project Administration Layer**

AI-powered project administration tools manage documentation, visual project databases, and scoping workflows. These features target the coordination overhead that multiplies when construction projects involve dozens of stakeholders who need access to current project information.

**Collaboration Infrastructure**

Unlimited internal and external viewer access comes standard across [all pricing tiers](https://plannerly.com/pricing), eliminating the per-seat cost barrier that typically restricts who can view project data. Multiple user roles support different permission levels while maintaining security through ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI Level 1 certifications.

The platform runs on AWS infrastructure and integrates with major construction and engineering tools, particularly Autodesk products. The [Autodesk partnership](https://www.autodesk.com/integrations/partner/plannerly) positions Plannerly as a management layer that orchestrates workflows across modeling tools rather than replacing them.

## Plannerly Buyer Personas

**End Users:** BIM managers and digital engineering professionals at mid-to-large construction and architecture firms who waste 8+ hours weekly managing fragmented BIM workflows across disconnected tools, costing teams $25K+ monthly in documentation rework and compliance errors. They need automated ISO 19650 compliance enforcement to eliminate manual model validation and reduce project scope miscommunication.

**Buyers:** Director of Digital Engineering or BIM Director at 100-500 person firms with $15-40K annual software budgets. They trigger purchases when ISO 19650 compliance becomes contractually mandated (particularly UK public sector) or when manual BIM execution planning creates project delays. Success means eliminating 6+ hours weekly spent on standards documentation and reducing model validation errors by 90%.

**Key Influencers:** Project managers concerned with delivery timelines, IT/infrastructure teams evaluating AWS compatibility and security certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2), and technical leads assessing file format interoperability across 80+ supported formats.

**Ideal Company Profile:** 100-500 employees in construction, architecture, or engineering sectors operating on projects requiring ISO 19650 compliance. Top fit indicators include multinational teams needing unlimited external viewer access without per-seat licensing, existing Autodesk tool adoption (BIM 360, Navisworks), complex project scoping requiring standardized BEP (BIM Execution Planning) workflows, and UK or European market focus where standards compliance is mandated.

## Plannerly Funding & Performance

Plannerly closed a [$4.12 million Series A](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/plannerly/__J-D8i-wylqGr6ep6bHt9LEW_h90IHPC0LOT2E74kBlA/funding-and-investors) round on April 30, 2025, led by Shadow Ventures. This represents the only verified financial data point available for the company.

No information exists in authoritative databases about earlier funding rounds, suggesting this may be the company's first institutional investment or that prior rounds were below standard reporting thresholds.

**Missing Metrics**

As a private company, Plannerly hasn't disclosed:

- Post-money valuation
- Revenue figures (current or historical)
- Annual recurring revenue (ARR)
- Customer count or growth rates
- Burn rate or runway
- Customer acquisition costs

The six-month gap between Series A and current date provides limited time to assess post-funding execution. Typical Series A metrics that would validate market traction—revenue growth, customer acquisition velocity, retention rates—remain unavailable through public channels.

For investors or strategic buyers, comprehensive due diligence requires direct engagement with the company or lead investor Shadow Ventures to obtain financial performance data.

## Plannerly Competitive Landscape

Plannerly competes in the BIM management space but positions itself as a specialized compliance and planning layer rather than a general construction management platform.

**Primary Competitors**

[Major players](https://thedigitalprojectmanager.com/tools/best-bim-project-management-software) include:

- **Autodesk BIM 360** \- Comprehensive cloud platform for construction project management with broad lifecycle capabilities
- **Autodesk Navisworks** \- Established clash detection and model coordination tool
- **Autodesk Revit** \- Leading BIM authoring platform for architectural and structural design
- **Tekla Structures** \- Detailed modeling platform with structural engineering focus
- **Dalux** \- BIM collaboration emphasizing field management

**Market Positioning**

Plannerly carved out a niche in ISO 19650 standards management. While Autodesk tools dominate general BIM workflows, the company's architecture centers entirely on compliance and BIM execution planning—not modeling or clash detection.

The [Autodesk partnership](https://www.autodesk.com/integrations/partner/plannerly) validates this coopetition approach: integrating with modeling tools while owning the management and compliance layer above them.

**Key Differentiators**

[ISO 19650-first](https://plannerly.com/) design distinguishes Plannerly from tools that support standards as features. The platform treats compliance as the organizing principle rather than an add-on.

The storage-based pricing with unlimited viewers contrasts sharply with per-seat enterprise licensing. This matters in construction where projects involve numerous external stakeholders.

Support for [80+ file formats](https://plannerly.com/product) provides broader interoperability than proprietary-focused platforms.

**Strategic Risk**

Direct competitors are dominated by Autodesk products, creating acquisition opportunity but also risk that Autodesk builds competing ISO 19650 features into existing platforms.

## Plannerly User Sentiment

Plannerly maintains no presence on enterprise review platforms. Comprehensive searches across G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, GetApp, ProductHunt, and Software Advice returned zero user reviews.

This absence suggests either limited market penetration, early adoption phase following the April 2025 Series A, or a customer base concentrated in private sales channels rather than self-service adoption.

For construction firms evaluating Plannerly, this creates validation challenges. Without independent user feedback on implementation complexity, support quality, or real-world performance, buyers must rely on direct vendor references and extended trial periods to assess product-market fit.

The review gap becomes particularly relevant given that construction software adoption carries high switching costs—teams invest significant time in training, data migration, and workflow integration.

## Plannerly Pricing

Plannerly monetizes through storage-based subscriptions rather than per-user seats—a structural departure from typical enterprise software pricing.

**Pricing Tiers**

| Tier | Storage | Viewer Access | Target Segment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | Limited | Unlimited | Testing/evaluation |
| Individual | 3 GB | Unlimited | Solo practitioners |
| Team | 100 GB | Unlimited | Small to mid-sized teams |
| Enterprise | 10 TB | Unlimited | Large organizations |

Specific dollar amounts for Individual and Team tiers aren't published. Enterprise [pricing requires](https://help.plannerly.com/en/article/73-plannerly-pricing-options-how-to-request-a-quotation-for-plannerly) quotation, indicating consultative sales for large accounts.

**Business Model Differentiator**

The [unlimited viewer](https://plannerly.com/pricing) model solves a real problem in construction: projects involve contractors, subcontractors, architects, engineers, and clients who all need visibility without companies paying $50-$100 per seat monthly. This removes the cost friction that typically restricts project stakeholder access.

Storage-based pricing makes sense for BIM workflows where file sizes balloon quickly, but creates different scaling dynamics than per-seat models. Revenue growth depends on customers storing more project data rather than adding users—potentially limiting revenue expansion compared to traditional SaaS pricing.

The model benefits customers with many collaborators but relatively modest storage needs. It penalizes customers with extensive project archives but smaller teams.
